answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a slashable identity bond: to join, each agent locks real collateral plus a unique attestation. An attacker wanting many fake identities must post a separate bond for every one, so cost scales linearly with the number of Sybils. Picture a raven scanning a frozen tundra from a stone terrace: each perch it claims costs actual value. If any node double-votes or forges an attestation, its bond is slashed, so amassing a large army becomes prohibitively expensive rather than free.
